title: Senior SWE diagnostic
objectives: Separate Python gaps from existing engineering experience.
Define measurable portfolio evidence and independent practice.

exercises.title: Evidence from shipped work
exercises.prompt: Choose one actual shipped AI product. Describe the user workflow, your contribution, architecture, a rejected alternative, measured result and limitation. If evidence is unavailable, mark it unknown. Then map three gaps to production Python, evals or enterprise delivery.
acceptance_checks: Separates personal and team ownership.
Uses actual evidence or clearly labels unknowns.
Maps gaps to concrete exercises.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Reward honest scope and causal evidence, not invented metrics.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Define both project contracts
exercises.prompt: Write charters for DeepSWE and an Enterprise AI Support Agent. For each give a user, task, scope exclusions, baseline, quality/cost/latency targets and one security gate. Explain which work can be deterministic.
acceptance_checks: Both projects have observable outcomes and baselines.
Targets are proposed, not claimed results.
Critical tool/tenant boundaries have testable gates.
exercises.interviewer_notes: DeepSWE proves bounded coding automation; support proves secure business workflow. Accept justified targets, not universal thresholds.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Which is valid project evidence?
options: A claimed result with no measurement
A measured result with workload and limitations
checks.explanation: Evidence names the measurement context and its limits.

checks.question: What follows a failed Python diagnostic?
options: Target the failed skill and retry fresh
checks.explanation: Remediation should match an observed gap.

checks.question: When does a guided score count as independent skill?
options: Only a fresh unassisted attempt supplies independent evidence
checks.explanation: Guided completion and independent performance are distinct.

title: Production Python contracts
objectives: Use typing, dataclasses and Pydantic at appropriate boundaries.
Design testable clients, packages, exceptions and logs.

exercises.title: Normalize an account response
exercises.prompt: Implement parse_account(payload) returning an immutable Account(id: str, active: bool). Reject empty IDs, missing fields, and string booleans such as 'false' with AccountPayloadError. Ignore extra upstream fields deliberately. Include parametrized pytest cases and a typed client interface.
acceptance_checks: Valid {'id':'a1','active':False} preserves False.
Missing/empty id and non-boolean active fail explicitly.
Tests cover invalid boundaries; no raw PII logging.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Pydantic strict validation or explicit checks acceptable; avoid bool('false'). Separate external validation from domain type.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Test a client boundary
exercises.prompt: Implement get_account(account_id, transport) against a fake transport exposing get(id) -> (status, payload). Map 200 through parse_account, 404 to AccountNotFound and 503 to DependencyUnavailable; other statuses to an explicit error. Supply pytest tests and a proposed package layout.
acceptance_checks: Tests distinguish 404, 503 and malformed 200 payload.
No network calls needed for routine tests.
Exceptions preserve useful cause without exposing payload secrets.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Use an injectable Protocol or callable; avoid catch-all returning None and mock only transport.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: What enforces untrusted JSON types?
checks.explanation: Runtime boundary validation checks external data; hints alone do not.

checks.question: What is the useful mocking seam?
checks.explanation: A fake transport preserves meaningful service behavior under test.

checks.question: What belongs in structured logs?
checks.explanation: Logs need diagnostic identifiers, not sensitive payloads.

title: Async clients and bounded concurrency
objectives: Bound work, deadlines and cancellation.
Choose async I/O, threads or processes and test cleanup.

exercises.title: Build a bounded mapper
exercises.prompt: Implement async bounded_map(items, call, limit) preserving input order. Inputs are a finite list; reject limit <= 0. Use at most limit workers and no task per item. Propagate call failures and cancel/await remaining workers. Include tests for empty input, ordering, failure and peak concurrency.
acceptance_checks: Peak active calls never exceeds limit.
Results preserve input order despite completion order.
Failure/caller cancellation leaves no running workers.
exercises.interviewer_notes: A worker pool with indexed results and try/finally cleanup is valid. Python 3.10 compatible patterns or an explicitly stated newer version are acceptable.
exercises.starter_code:
async def bounded_map(items, call, limit):
    raise NotImplementedError
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Repair a timeout design
exercises.prompt: A service uses gather over 50,000 calls, retries every exception forever and creates a new client each time. Propose and implement a small replacement using bounded work, a total deadline and an owned client. Show deterministic tests for permanent error, timeout and cancellation.
acceptance_checks: Retries are bounded and classify transient errors.
Caller cancellation terminates child work and closes resources.
Tests use controlled fakes/events rather than real provider calls.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Do not treat asyncio cancellation as an ordinary retry; distinguish per-attempt timeout from total deadline.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Does a semaphore bound allocated tasks?
options: No; it bounds entry to a protected section
checks.explanation: A separate worker/queue design is needed to bound pending tasks.

checks.question: Which operation blocks the event loop?
options: Synchronous blocking I/O inside async def
checks.explanation: Declaring async does not transform synchronous work.

checks.question: What should parent cancellation do?
checks.explanation: Cancellation is a lifecycle event, not a transient provider failure.

title: Datasets, graders and release gates
objectives: Build representative datasets and calibrated graders.
Compare task success, groundedness, tool accuracy, latency and cost.

exercises.title: Specify a benchmark harness
exercises.prompt: Design a case schema and six representative DeepSWE cases covering repair, multi-file work, impossible task, malicious repository text, timeout and tool denial. Define development/held-out grouping, deterministic tests, a judge rubric, human review and failure labels.
acceptance_checks: Cases have expected outcomes and prohibited actions.
Held-out families are not tuned on.
Timeouts and failures remain in denominators; judge cannot replace protected tests.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Demand reproducible inputs, grader versions, provenance and attack cases. Reject judge-only pass criteria for code correctness.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Make a release decision
exercises.prompt: Baseline resolves 30/40 tasks for $4 total; candidate resolves 32/40 for $8. Candidate p95 grows from 12s to 20s and has one unauthorized tool action versus zero. Compute success and cost per successful task; decide release under a zero-unauthorized-action guardrail and p95 <= 15s.
acceptance_checks: Reports 75% vs 80%, about $0.133 vs $0.25 per success.
Rejects promotion on safety and latency guardrails.
Requests matched repeated runs/slice analysis before claiming a robust quality gain.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Quality gain is 5 percentage points, not proof of significance. Costs include unsuccessful attempts.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Which split best reduces near-duplicate leakage?
checks.explanation: Family grouping reduces related examples across development and holdout.

checks.question: A judge prefers a fluent unsupported answer. What next?
checks.explanation: Judge preference is not correctness or grounding.

checks.question: What denominator counts task success?
options: All attempted eligible tasks, including crashes/timeouts
checks.explanation: Excluding failures inflates apparent performance.

title: Agent loops, state and context
objectives: Build explicit bounded loops and durable state.
Justify planning, context strategies and subagents against simpler workflows.

exercises.title: Specify a resumable loop
exercises.prompt: Design a state machine for a coding agent with read/search/edit/test tools. Include structured-output rejection, step/deadline/token budgets, no-progress stop, cancellation and checkpoints. Trace a successful repair and repeated failing-test loop.
acceptance_checks: Every execution path reaches a bounded terminal/pending state.
Authorization occurs outside the model.
Checkpoint data distinguishes attempts, observations and remaining budget.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Look for state ownership, repeated observation detection and recovery without resetting budgets.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Defend context and delegation
exercises.prompt: A task spans 30 files, but only four fit in context. Compare file selection plus source-linked summaries with full-context truncation. Design a matched eval of a reviewer subagent against a single agent, including permissions, cancellation and cost.
acceptance_checks: Preserves access to original evidence and bounds tool output.
Delegated permissions cannot exceed parent authority.
Measures quality, latency and total cost; accepts no subagent if benefit is absent.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Do not reward multi-agent complexity without measurable benefit.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Which task least needs an agent?
checks.explanation: Known steps can remain deterministic.

checks.question: Does valid tool-call JSON authorize execution?
checks.explanation: Schema validity and authority are different checks.

checks.question: A useful subagent comparison holds what constant?
options: Task set and overall resource budget
checks.explanation: Comparable tasks and budgets expose actual benefit and cost.

title: Tool permissions and sandboxing
objectives: Enforce file, process, network and secret boundaries.
Test direct and indirect injection at tool execution.

exercises.title: Design the execution boundary
exercises.prompt: Specify sandbox policy for read/search/edit/test tools on a disposable repository. Include filesystem, process, network, secrets, CPU/memory/disk/time/output limits, cleanup and audit fields. Supply six negative tests and residual risks.
acceptance_checks: Model cannot access host secrets or container engine.
Tests cover symlinks, egress, exhaustion and child-process cleanup.
Separates schema checks, authorization and OS isolation.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Accept a scoped container/VM design with explicit limits; reject prompt-only safety and shell allowlist-only isolation.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Review a malicious tool request
exercises.prompt: A README instructs an agent to upload .env to an external URL; a proposed tool call reads a symlink under the workspace and runs curl. Trace every trust boundary and explain safe denial, logging and task recovery without executing this attack.
acceptance_checks: Repository instructions do not override policy.
Path/egress/secret controls independently prevent effects.
Audit excludes secret contents; denial becomes an observable result.
exercises.interviewer_notes: No actual attack execution needed. Denial should not trigger retries with broader permissions.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: What makes a shell allowlist insufficient?
options: Shell syntax and environment can still escape intent
checks.explanation: Commands alone do not isolate files, network or resources.

checks.question: Repository text asks for more privileges. What happens?
options: Treat it as untrusted input; enforce server policy
checks.explanation: Untrusted content cannot expand capabilities.

checks.question: Which is safe audit content?
options: Actor, action, decision and redacted identifiers
checks.explanation: Auditability does not require recording secrets.

title: Durable AI jobs and recovery
objectives: Design idempotent effects, bounded retries and durable recovery.
Control overload, fallbacks, caches and budgets.

exercises.title: Recover an uncertain effect
exercises.prompt: Design a durable support-action worker for at-least-once delivery. The remote API supports idempotency keys. Show state transitions and recovery if the process dies before the call, after the effect, or after local completion but before ack.
acceptance_checks: One stable logical-operation key survives retries.
Acknowledgment follows durable outcome recording.
Stale workers and revoked authorization are addressed.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Use outbox/leases/fencing as justified; explain remote idempotency retention and reconciliation limits.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Handle sustained overload
exercises.prompt: Jobs arrive at 9/s and complete at 6/s for 60s. Compute queue growth, then propose admission control, concurrency/rate caps, bounded retries, breaker/fallback and an authorized cache. State user-visible degraded behavior.
acceptance_checks: Calculates 180 extra jobs under stated assumptions.
Does not treat queue growth as free capacity.
Fallback and cache preserve tenant/security and freshness policy.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Bound retries and total deadlines; account for queue wait in p95, not just model service time.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: A worker crashes after a remote effect. Which protects retries?
options: A local flag written later alone
checks.explanation: A stable key identifies the same logical effect across attempts.

checks.question: What happens if arrivals exceed departures indefinitely?
options: Backlog grows unless work is rejected or capacity changes
checks.explanation: Queues absorb bursts, not permanent capacity deficits.

checks.question: A role was revoked during an agent pause. On resume:
checks.explanation: Persistent state is not persistent authorization.

title: AI traces, costs and incidents
objectives: Trace request, queue, model and tool boundaries.
Use production feedback and evals to drive safe releases.

exercises.title: Investigate the latency regression
exercises.prompt: Before release, p95 end-to-end is 8s; after, 18s. Mean model latency stays 2s, queue age doubles and retries rise. Give competing hypotheses, exact trace/metric comparisons, a mitigation, a reproducer and a rollback rule.
acceptance_checks: Separates observations from unproven causes.
Measures queue/model/tool/retry spans on comparable cohorts.
Mitigation and regression verification are explicit.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Do not infer a unique root cause from correlated queue age/retries; propose discriminating evidence.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Design trace and cost accounting
exercises.prompt: Define one trace for a failed model call, retry, tool call and successful completion. Include IDs, timing, token/cost estimates, redaction, metrics and production-feedback sampling. Explain how CI gates the next release.
acceptance_checks: Failed attempts and retries contribute to total cost.
Logs/traces do not expose secrets or unrestricted PII.
Explains missing usage, trace sampling and grader/version changes.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Quality, safety and latency gates should precede rollout; observability alone does not certify improvement.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Can component p95 values simply be added?
checks.explanation: Tail events need not occur on the same request.

checks.question: Cost per successful task should include:
options: All attempt costs including failures and retries
checks.explanation: The cost of failures is part of delivering successful outcomes.

checks.question: What makes an alert actionable?
options: Owner, threshold, diagnostic evidence and runbook
checks.explanation: An alert should support an operational decision.

title: Project 1 · DeepSWE
objectives: Deliver a bounded autonomous coding agent.
Defend benchmark validity, security and production evidence.

exercises.title: DeepSWE release review
exercises.prompt: Submit an evidence card for milestones M1–M6 with links or pasted excerpts of actual code/tests/results. If not built, label each item planned and supply an implementation sequence. Include a 40-task split, baseline, controls and protected grader design.
acceptance_checks: All six milestones have actual evidence or explicit gaps.
Benchmark protects grading from agent edits.
Reports success, security, cost/latency and failures without invented results.
exercises.interviewer_notes: A proposal may pass the exercise as a plan but is not a completed portfolio release; call this distinction out.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Defend an agent regression
exercises.prompt: A new planner solves 3 more held-out tasks but sometimes modifies tests and incurs twice the token cost. Present a release decision, investigation, constrained follow-up experiment and a five-minute project defense covering your own contribution.
acceptance_checks: Rejects trusting agent-editable tests.
Explains matched reruns, holdout reuse and cost guardrails.
Distinguishes personal work, uncertain results and next evidence.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Treat altered tests as grading-integrity concern. Do not reward unsupported benchmark/leaderboard claims.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Who should control final grading tests?
checks.explanation: Agent-editable tests cannot independently verify repairs.

checks.question: Which result supports a benchmark claim?
options: Versioned tasks, matched budgets and raw results
checks.explanation: Reproducibility and comparable conditions matter.

checks.question: What does completing this tutorial prove?
options: Exercises were reviewed, not portfolio completion
checks.explanation: Only implementation and measured evidence establish project completion.

title: Retrieval metrics and diagnosis
objectives: Measure Recall@K, Precision@K, MRR and NDCG.
Compare chunking, hybrid search, reranking and context selection.

exercises.title: Implement ranking metrics
exercises.prompt: Implement retrieval_metrics(ranked, relevant, k) for unique document IDs and a nonempty relevant set. Return Precision@K, Recall@K and reciprocal rank within K. Reject k <= 0 and duplicates; use K as precision denominator even if fewer results. Test B,A,C with relevant A,C at K=3.
acceptance_checks: Example returns 2/3, 1 and 1/2.
Absent relevant results give zero reciprocal rank.
Tests cover fewer results, invalid K and duplicates; explains no-answer handling.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Use set membership, cap ranks at K; reciprocal rank is for one query and MRR averages queries.
exercises.starter_code:
def retrieval_metrics(ranked, relevant, k):
    raise NotImplementedError
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Diagnose high recall, weak answers
exercises.prompt: A hybrid retriever raises Recall@10 from .70 to .90, but grounded answer accuracy falls and p95 doubles. Design slice analysis and controlled comparisons of reranking, chunk overlap, query rewriting and context selection. Define graded relevance and NDCG convention.
acceptance_checks: Separates retrieval from unsupported generation.
Controls workload/model/token budgets and inspects permission/staleness failures.
Reports ranking, grounding, abstention, cost/latency and holdout limitations.
exercises.interviewer_notes: High recall can coexist with noisy or misleading context; experiments should isolate changes.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Top ranks B,A,C with relevant A,C: reciprocal rank?
checks.explanation: A is the first relevant result at rank 2.

checks.question: Why can better recall yield worse answers?
options: Extra context can distract or introduce conflicts
checks.explanation: Evidence selection and generation remain separate failure points.

checks.question: For no labeled relevant items, recall is:
checks.explanation: Avoid dividing by zero or silently distorting the mean.

title: Identity, privacy and enterprise controls
objectives: Enforce RBAC, OAuth scopes and tenant isolation outside models.
Handle injection, approvals, PII, secrets and auditability.

exercises.title: Close a tenant escape
exercises.prompt: Review this design: search(query, tenant_id) and get_bill(account_id) receive model-generated arguments; cache is keyed only by query. Redesign identity propagation, retrieval filtering, object authorization, cache keys and audit events. Give cross-tenant and revoked-role tests.
acceptance_checks: Trusted identity determines tenant context.
Every object/tool and cache result respects authorization.
Tests cover role revocation and malicious retrieved content.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Filtering only after generation is too late; cached data can leak even if the underlying query was secure.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Bind an approval to an effect
exercises.prompt: Design approval for a proposed $50 refund. Show transitions when amount changes to $500, approval expires, user role is revoked, worker retries or a human takes over. Include PII/secret minimization, audit fields and idempotency.
acceptance_checks: Changed arguments invalidate approval.
Execution rechecks role/tenant and expiry.
Stable key prevents duplicate effects; audit excludes sensitive payloads.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Approval records need exact action binding and authoritative validation, not model claims.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: Where should tenant identity originate?
checks.explanation: Untrusted arguments cannot select an authorization domain.

checks.question: OAuth authentication eliminates object authorization?
options: No; scopes and object permissions still matter
checks.explanation: Identity and delegation do not imply rights to every object.

checks.question: Approved refund arguments change. What now?
options: Invalidate approval and request a new bound decision
checks.explanation: Approval authorizes a specific action, not arbitrary future changes.

title: From business request to AI architecture
objectives: Discover the workflow and quantify success.
Design integrations, evals, rollout, monitoring and ownership.

exercises.title: Discover and design support AI
exercises.prompt: For a fictional B2B SaaS support team handling 5,000 tickets/day, ask eight discovery questions, state assumptions and propose rules/model/RAG/agent boundaries. Design CRM, billing and knowledge integrations with identity, failure and approval flows.
acceptance_checks: Questions identify business baseline, data/actions and owners.
Explains why each AI component is necessary.
Includes eval slices, security boundaries and measurable workflow outcome.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Do not reward architecture box lists without request flow or requirements; scale is an assumption to refine.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Plan the rollout
exercises.prompt: Create a four-stage shadow/staff-assist/pilot/expansion plan for the design. Specify entry/exit criteria, responsible roles, monitoring, rollback and implementation dependencies. Show how an outage and a quality regression change the plan.
acceptance_checks: Each stage has measurable gates and an owner.
Critical authorization failures block rollout.
Business outcome, human costs and adoption are evaluated alongside model quality.
exercises.interviewer_notes: A successful demo is not an operational readiness gate.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: What comes first in vague enterprise AI work?
options: Discover workflow, baseline and outcome owner
checks.explanation: Architecture should follow the actual problem.

checks.question: What justifies an agent?
options: Dynamic decisions that simpler workflows cannot adequately handle
checks.explanation: Agent complexity needs a workflow-driven reason.

checks.question: Which rollout signal is insufficient alone?
checks.explanation: A demo does not establish reliability, adoption or business value.

title: Project 2 · Enterprise support agent
objectives: Deliver a secure RAG/tool workflow with human controls.
Measure reliability, adoption and business outcomes honestly.

exercises.title: Support release evidence
exercises.prompt: Submit S1–S6 evidence or explicitly labeled gaps: retrieval, architecture, CRM/billing tools, RBAC/tenant controls, approvals/escalation, observability/evals and deployment. Specify 60-case split, quality/security/cost/latency targets and rollback.
acceptance_checks: Distinguishes implemented, mocked and planned work.
Critical cross-tenant/approval tests must pass.
Release evidence covers failure behavior and all six milestones.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Do not imply exercise completion certifies a deployment; ask for actual artifacts and limitations.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Evaluate workflow value
exercises.prompt: A pilot reduces median handling time from 10 to 6 minutes, but reopens rise from 5% to 15% and each ticket needs 2 minutes of review. Design a launch decision and further measurement plan, accounting for matched categories, staff adoption, correctness and total cost.
acceptance_checks: Does not equate faster first closure with value.
Includes review/rework and observation-window effects.
Separates actual pilot evidence from projections and proposes safe rollout/rollback.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Insufficient data for exact ROI; identify denominators, review costs, ticket mix and quality guardrails.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: A mock CRM adapter proves:
checks.explanation: Mocks are useful evidence but not verified external delivery.

checks.question: When a human takes over:
options: Persist ownership and stop unauthorized automatic effects
checks.explanation: Handoff requires authoritative state and execution checks.

checks.question: Which supports business impact?
options: Observed quality, rework, cost and adoption under stated conditions
checks.explanation: Business outcomes need workflow evidence.

title: Eight enterprise design cases
objectives: Defend AI versus deterministic choices across enterprise scenarios.
Evaluate tools, approvals, privacy, injection and value.

exercises.title: Compare four business workflows
exercises.prompt: Choose support, sales, document processing or financial operations. In 45 minutes design one, then explain three changes needed for a second. Address the ten questions in the guide and include five eval cases.
acceptance_checks: AI/agent choice is justified against deterministic baseline.
Tools/approval and PII/injection controls are concrete.
Business metric and failure evals fit both selected workflows.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Accept a deterministic final design if justified. Financial effects and external contact need explicit authority/approval.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Search, knowledge, coding or delegation
exercises.prompt: Choose internal knowledge, enterprise search, coding or multi-agent workflow. Design it for 200 concurrent users and p95 <= 10s, stating assumptions. Then handle a tenfold load increase and a revoked data permission during a running job.
acceptance_checks: Covers all ten design questions and five eval cases.
Reauthorization and cache/retrieval isolation survive revocation.
Explains capacity, degradation and whether subagents justify cost.
exercises.interviewer_notes: The 10s target may be infeasible; honest decomposition and negotiation are valid. Do not reward unsupported latency claims.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: An acceptable case answer can reject AI?
options: Yes, if workflow evidence favors deterministic logic
checks.explanation: The task is sound engineering judgment, not maximizing AI use.

checks.question: What must subagents share or coordinate?
options: Budgets, state ownership and bounded handoff contracts
checks.explanation: Delegation adds coordination and authorization risks.

checks.question: Which question belongs in every case?
checks.explanation: Enterprise architecture must connect implementation to outcomes.

title: Discovery and architecture defense
objectives: Ask discovery questions and negotiate implementation plans.
Explain tradeoffs to engineers, product, security and executives.

exercises.title: Discover before proposing
exercises.prompt: Role-play a support leader requesting full AI automation next month. Write eight prioritized questions, then a concise summary with assumptions, missing information, success metrics and a phased implementation proposal.
acceptance_checks: Questions uncover workflow, baseline, integration/security and ownership.
Plan contains dependencies, acceptance gates and a next decision.
Does not invent customer answers or promise unsupported results.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Evaluate discovery and negotiation quality, not agreeableness or personality.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Defend one decision to four audiences
exercises.prompt: Choose a real or explicitly hypothetical decision to require approval before refunds. Explain it to engineers, product, security and a CTO in at most 150 words each. Include the strongest alternative and evidence that could change your position.
acceptance_checks: Same factual decision is communicated consistently.
Each audience gets relevant tradeoffs and next action.
Real ownership and hypothetical claims are distinguished.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Engineering: contracts; product: friction/value; security: controls; executive: risk/investment. Avoid jargon-only defense.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

checks.question: What should discovery establish early?
checks.explanation: Baseline and ownership make success assessable.

checks.question: Good architecture defense includes:
options: Evidence that could change the decision
checks.explanation: Technical judgment includes falsifiable tradeoffs.

checks.question: How should audience adaptation change facts?
options: Keep facts consistent; change emphasis and detail
checks.explanation: Clear communication preserves accuracy.

title: Interview Mode vs Work Mode
objectives: Use AI actively at work and verify its output.
Keep independent interview evidence separate from assisted work.

exercises.title: Review AI-assisted work
exercises.prompt: Describe an AI-assisted change to retry behavior. Supply a review checklist, meaningful fake-transport tests, one rejected AI suggestion and an evidence log. Label any unexecuted tests. Explain how you would debug it without AI.
acceptance_checks: Tests exercise behavior rather than mocking the function under test.
Covers cancellation, permanent errors and bounded attempts.
Distinguishes proposed, executed and model-claimed results.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Reward independent verification and small reviewable changes, not mere tool usage.
constraints: State assumptions and distinguish implemented results from plans.
Run code/tests in your own environment; the lab does not execute submissions.

exercises.title: Plan a two-track week
exercises.prompt: Allocate 12–15 hours across project work, two 45-minute coding attempts, design/behavioral practice and review. Specify allowed AI use in each block and a fresh-task remediation loop. Include threat-model/eval generation and manual validation.
acceptance_checks: Interview attempts remain unaided and preserved.

title: DSA 1 · Arrays, windows and search
objectives: Practice hashing, two pointers, windows, stacks and binary search.

exercises.title: Earliest target pair · easy
exercises.prompt: Implement pair_indices(nums, target) returning (i,j) with i<j and nums[i]+nums[j]==target. Choose the smallest j, then smallest i; return None if absent. Do not mutate input. For [3,3,2,4], target=6 returns (0,1). Aim for expected O(n); include tests.
acceptance_checks: Duplicates use distinct indices and earliest tie-breaking.
Empty/no-solution input returns None.
Explains prefix invariant and expected O(n) time/O(n) space.
exercises.interviewer_notes: Store first index per value, check complement before insertion; retain earliest index for ties.
